messages.subject_clean: problem installing RHIPE package into R (ben cotton)
messages.body_plain:
---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: ben.c...@lehman.com <benjami...@lehman.com>
Date: Mon, Nov 30, 2009 at 1:46 PM
Subject: problem installing RHIPE package into R
To: sg...@purdue.edu

Hi Saptarshi,

We are very interested in exploring the potential of using RHIPE to
help us bridge our R-based Risk Analytics platform to interface with
new exttremely large (13+ TB)  Hadoop-based data sources.    We have
downloaded the RHIPE_0.51.tar.gz bundled, confirmed all the
pre-requisites as documented at the RHIPE web site, but encounter the
attached error when we execute

R CMD INSTALL Rhipe_0.51.tar.gz

Are we doing anything wrong?    Also, is there any RHIPE user mailing
list and/or user support forum that you could point us to?  Would you
be available/willing to assist us installing RHIPE in our R/Hadoop
environemnt?

many thanks for any consideration to help, we would like to take a
strong look at RHIPE and are excited about its potential,

Ben
212-377-1514

* Installing to library â/usr/lib64/R/libraryâ
* Installing *source* package âRhipeâ ...
checking for gcc... gcc -std=gnu99
checking for C compiler default output file name... a.out
checking whether the C compiler works... yes
checking whether we are cross compiling... no
checking for suffix of executables...
checking for suffix of object files... o
checking whether we are using the GNU C compiler... yes
checking whether gcc -std=gnu99 accepts -g... yes
checking for gcc -std=gnu99 option to accept ISO C89... none needed
configure: creating ./config.status
config.status: creating src/Makevars
** libs
g++ -I/usr/lib64/R/include  -I/usr/local/include    -fpic  -O2 -I. -O3
  `pkg-config --cflags protobuf` -Wall -c display.cc -o display.o
g++ -I/usr/lib64/R/include  -I/usr/local/include    -fpic  -O2 -I. -O3
  `pkg-config --cflags protobuf` -Wall -c main.cc -o main.o
main.cc:58: error: second argument of âint main(int, char*)â should be âchar **â
make: *** [main.o] Error 1
ERROR: compilation failed for package âRhipeâ
* Removing â/usr/lib64/R/library/Rhipeâ

-
